evidence.observation: The dependency path is checkout-web -> payment-api -> auth-gateway; AUTH-2026-0318 was deployed to auth-gateway at 14:05Z and changed the issuer and JWKS cache namespace.
At 14:10Z, checkout-web had an 18.7% HTTP 401 rate and payment-api had a 21.2% HTTP 401 rate; auth-gateway had a 28.4% HTTP 401 rate with notes indicating a JWKS cache miss and issuer mismatch.

After the deployment, auth-gateway fell back from the partner-v2 JWKS namespace and rejected partner-v2 tokens because only partner-v1 was allowed. The log identifies reverting AUTH-2026-0318 or restoring partner-v2 as rollback candidates.
payment-api logged issuer_not_allowed from auth-gateway and rejected request req-8812 as invalid_issuer before reaching the order database.
checkout-web reported a 401 from payment-api and an invalid issuer for checkout session cko-17; static assets recovered but checkout remained blocked.

excluded_red_herrings.why_not_primary: Query p95 remained 35 ms with zero errors, and no failed checkout transaction reached orders-db.
The metric notes isolate the failures to images, while checkout authentication failures occurred through payment-api and static assets served normally after retry.
These are downstream symptoms; checkout-web logs identify payment-api as the failing upstream, and payment-api identifies auth-gateway issuer rejection.

recommended_next_steps: Immediately restore allowed_issuers to include partner-v2 or revert AUTH-2026-0318, following the documented rollback candidate.
Verify auth-gateway JWKS cache namespace and issuer configuration agree on partner-v2, then confirm successful token validation.
Run a synthetic checkout through checkout-web and confirm payment-api returns success, HTTP 401 rates return to baseline, and a transaction reaches orders-db.
Review the deployment configuration and add a pre-deploy issuer/JWKS compatibility check and alert on issuer_not_allowed spikes.
